items.title: Accidental Payment Scam: Don't Send Money Back
items.summary:
You get an unexpected payment — Venmo, Cash App, Zelle, or a text
message says someone sent you money by mistake. Then a message follows:
"They accidentally sent you money, please send it back." If you send it
back, you lose. The original payment may be fraudulent and get reversed
by the bank, but the money you voluntarily sent is gone for good.

What to do: Do not send money back. Leave the funds untouched and
contact your bank or payment service through its official app, website,
or customer-service number. Do not trust screenshots or messages from
the sender as proof. Avoid clicking links from strangers — they lead to
fake login pages.

This matters: Scammers use stolen cards or hacked accounts to send the
initial payment. When the real owner disputes it, the bank reverses...

items.title: Windows 11 November 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes 1,252 vulnerabilities including an exploited zero-day
items.summary: Install KB5132061 from Windows Update (Settings > Windows Update) — it patches 68 critical flaws and one actively exploited zero-day in Windows 11 24H2, 25H2, and 26H2. Supported versions get build 26300.9974 (26H2), 26200.9974 (25H2), or 26100.9974 (24H2 Enterprise/Education).

items.title: AI Voice Clone Scams Are Calling — Hang Up and Call Back on a Known Number
items.summary:
AI voice clone scams are calling people right now. The caller sounds exactly like a family member — a grandchild, a child, a spouse — and says they're in trouble. They need money immediately for bail, a car repair, a medical emergency. It's not them. Scammers use AI to clone voices from social media videos.

The call feels real because the voice is real — it's a copy of someone you love. The scammer pressures you to act fast, send money, don't tell anyone.

What to do: Hang up. Call the person back on a number you know is theirs. If you can't reach them, call another family member to check. Never send money or gift cards based on a surprise call, no matter how real the voice sounds.

items.title: Microsoft November 2026 Patch Tuesday Fixes 600+ Security Flaws Including Outlook Zero-Day
items.summary: Install the November 2026 Windows 11 cumulative update (KB5132061 for 24H2/25H2/26H2) via Settings > Windows Update to patch the actively exploited Outlook vulnerability the vulnerability-2026-124194 and 600+ other security flaws.

items.title: Microsoft Defender Is Enough for Most Lake City Home Users — Free and Built Into Windows 11
items.summary: Open Windows Security (press Start and type "Windows Security"). Microsoft Defender antivirus is on by default, updates automatically, and protects against viruses and ransomware without any subscription.

items.title: Holiday Shopping Scams Hide in Your Search Results
items.summary:
Holiday shopping scams are hiding at the top of your search results.

When you search for a gift, the first links are often paid ads from scammers — not the real store. Click one and you could hand over your credit card or personal information to a fake site that looks almost identical to the real thing.

What to do: Scroll past the top results. The organic listings below the ads are ranked by relevance, not by who paid the most. Better yet, type the store's web address directly into your browser. If you're not sure about a site, search the company name plus "complaint" or "scam" before you buy.

items.title: Windows 11 26H2 Is Free — Check If Your PC Qualifies with PC Health Check
items.summary: Windows 11 26H2 is a free upgrade for eligible PCs. Open Settings → Windows Update → Check for updates, or download the free PC Health Check app at aka.ms/GetPCHealthCheckApp to see if your hardware meets the requirements (TPM 2.0, Secure Boot, 4 GB RAM, 64 GB storage). PCs on 24H2 or 25H2 upgrade with one restart via enablement package KB5121794; older versions (23H2, 22H2, Windows 10) use the Windows 11 Installation Assistant from microsoft.com/windows11 for a full upgrade. (Source: Microsoft Support, Techdows, September–November 2026)

items.title: Firefox 160 Adds On-Device Speech-to-Text in 40 Languages — No Cloud Needed
items.summary: Firefox 160 (released November 10, 2026) includes the SpeechRecognition API for real-time, on-device speech-to-text in 40 languages — works offline, no data sent to servers. Update free at firefox.com or via Menu → Help → About Firefox. Also new: Mini Window for always-on-top tabs, Picture-in-Picture speed controls (0.25×–2×), and a "Never allow" button to block sites from repeatedly asking to handle mailto: links. (Source: Firefox 160 Release Notes, November 10, 2026)
